name: AirSense
tagline: Hyperlocal air quality: know before you breathe
problem: One official station often stands in for a whole town
Homes by highways, industry and burning fields have no local data
Cheap sensors are noisy, drift and over-read in humid air
People find out the air was bad only after breathing it

stats.label: premature deaths a year linked to air pollution (approx., WHO)
Indian cities in the National Clean Air Programme (approx., NCAP)
of unhealthy hours the single station missed (our demo town)

solution: Calibrates every low-cost sensor against a reference station
Catches stuck, spiking and drifting sensors automatically
CPCB AQI heat map with uncertainty for any spot in town
24-hour forecast with personal alerts and the best time to run

architecture: 25 PM sensors + 2 reference stations -> hourly CSV
calibration.py -> kappa-Koehler humidity fix + MLR per sensor
faults.py -> stuck, spike, drift vs neighbours' median
aqi.py -> CPCB sub-indices, averaging and validity rules
interpolate.py / forecast.py / sources.py -> map, 24 h, source hints
app.py stdlib JSON API -> vanilla JS canvas map + SVG charts
algorithms: CPCB piecewise-linear sub-index - India National AQI
kappa-Koehler growth + multiple linear regression - calibration
Robust z-scores (median/MAD) - stuck, spike and drift detection
IDW and ordinary kriging with fitted variogram - heat map + uncertainty
Seasonal profile + AR + weather regression - 24-hour forecast
Pollution rose + upwind CWT rays - likely sources
tech: Canvas heat map, hand-drawn SVG charts
innovation: Turns ~Rs 5k sensors into near-reference data with explainable maths
The network checks itself: every flag names the rule that fired
Every map pixel has an uncertainty, not just a colour
Forecast-driven personal alerts before exposure, not after
